oauthNotes: Two app types: OAuth apps and GitHub Apps. Both are registered in Developer settings without review.

composio.note: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for GitHub, so development can start without registering your own. A custom OAuth app is needed for your own branding on the consent screen, dedicated quota, or scopes beyond Composio's defaults.

summary: Registering a GitHub OAuth app is self-service and takes minutes, with no review before any GitHub user can authorise it. The work is in choosing between an OAuth app and a GitHub App, and in handling organisations that restrict OAuth app access by default.

verdict.headline: Testing is available within minutes. Production access requires no review: any GitHub user can authorise the app as soon as it is registered.
verdict.biggestRisk: New organisations restrict OAuth app access by default, so an organisation owner must approve the app before members can grant it access to organisation resources.

paths.name: OAuth app
paths.whenThisApplies: The agent acts as the signed-in user across everything that user can access. This is what Composio's GitHub toolkit uses.

activeEffort.basis: Registration, credentials and a test authorisation.

waitTime.basis: No provider review on this path.

timeToProduction.basis: No review step is documented. Registration is self-service.

steps.title: Register a new OAuth app
steps.detail: In Settings, open Developer settings, then OAuth apps, and select New OAuth App. Enter the application name, homepage URL and callback URL.
gotchas: Register the app under an organisation account, not a personal one, so ownership does not depend on one person.

steps.title: Generate a client secret
steps.detail: Generate the secret and add the client ID and secret to a Composio auth config.

steps.title: Select the minimum scopes
steps.detail: The agent proposes the narrowest scopes for the tools the product uses. See Prepared materials.

steps.title: Run a test authorisation
steps.detail: Authorise with a test account and confirm the granted scopes. PKCE is supported with the S256 method only.

paths.name: GitHub App
paths.whenThisApplies: The product needs fine-grained, per-repository permissions or short-lived tokens. GitHub recommends this type in general.

timeToFirstLogin.basis: Estimate. More configuration than an OAuth app. No direct source.

waitTime.basis: No provider review on this path.

timeToProduction.basis: Estimate. No review step is documented.

steps.title: Register a GitHub App
steps.detail: In Developer settings, register a GitHub App and select its repository and organisation permissions.

links.label: GitHub Apps and OAuth apps compared

steps.title: Install the app and test
steps.detail: Install the app on an account or organisation you own. Installation access tokens expire after 1 hour.
gotchas: Confirm that your integration layer supports GitHub App installation tokens before choosing this type.

requirements.detail: The app is owned by a user or an organisation. Each can own up to 100 OAuth apps.
Up to 10 callback URLs can be registered.

nuances.title: Organisations restrict OAuth apps by default
nuances.detail: New organisations have OAuth app access restrictions enabled. Members can authorise the app, but it cannot reach organisation resources until an owner approves it.

nuances.title: Rate limit is 5,000 requests per hour per user
nuances.detail: OAuth tokens use the authorising user's limit, shared with that user's other tokens. OAuth app limits do not scale with usage.

nuances.title: Ten tokens per user, app and scope combination
nuances.detail: Issuing an eleventh token revokes an existing one, so store and reuse tokens.

nuances.title: Token expiry is optional for OAuth apps
nuances.detail: OAuth apps can be configured to issue user access tokens that expire after eight hours. With expiry enabled, refresh tokens expire after six months without use.

nuances.title: GitHub recommends GitHub Apps
nuances.detail: GitHub Apps use fine-grained permissions and let the user choose which repositories the app can access.

blockers.symptom: Organisation repositories are missing after authorisation
blockers.cause: The organisation has OAuth app access restrictions enabled and has not approved the app.
blockers.fix: Ask the user to request approval from an organisation owner on the authorisation screen, or have an owner approve the app in the organisation's third-party access settings.

blockers.symptom: A stored token stops working unexpectedly
blockers.cause: More than ten tokens were issued for the same user, app and scope combination.
blockers.fix: Reuse the stored token instead of re-authorising on each run.

blockers.cause: The redirect URL's host and port must match the registered callback URL.
blockers.fix: Register the exact Composio callback URL as a callback URL.

handoffKit.title: Registration form values
handoffKit.content:
Application name: <Your product name>
Homepage URL: https://<yourdomain>
Application description: <One-line description shown to users>
Authorization callback URL: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback
Enable Device Flow: off, unless the product runs without a browser

handoffKit.title: OAuth app or GitHub App
handoffKit.content:
Choose an OAuth app when: the agent acts as the user everywhere the user has access, and Composio's GitHub toolkit is used as provided.
Choose a GitHub App when: customers require per-repository access, short-lived tokens (1 hour) or rate limits that scale with the installation.
GitHub's stated position: GitHub Apps are preferred in general.

handoffKit.title: Connect the OAuth app to Composio
handoffKit.content:
1. In the Composio dashboard, open Auth Configs and create one for GitHub using OAuth2 with your own developer credentials.
2. Enter the client ID and client secret. Set the redirect URI to https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback
3. Pass the auth config ID (ac_...) in your session's authConfigs, keyed by toolkit. Creating the auth config alone does not apply it.
Reference: https://docs.composio.dev/docs/authentication/custom-app-vs-managed-app
